title: Decomposing Language Models Into Understandable Components
excerpt: Anthropic researchers describe methods for breaking language model computations into interpretable subgraphs and features, aiming to make internal mechanisms legible rather than treating models as monolithic black boxes. The work is early-stage relative to frontier model scale and focuses on Anthropic's interpretability toolchain.
author: Anthropic

title: Circuits: Early Vision
excerpt: Chris Olah and collaborators present early circuits work tracing how vision networks compose curve detectors, high-low frequency contrast, and object fragments into hierarchical features. The analysis is InceptionV1-specific and predates transformer-centric circuit research.
author: Chris Olah et al.

title: Multimodal Neurons in Artificial Neural Networks
excerpt: Gabriel Goh, Nick Cammarata, and colleagues show CLIP neurons that respond to abstract concepts across images and text—demonstrating emergent multimodal semantics in contrastive models. The findings are CLIP-specific and do not establish general multimodal interpretability methods.
author: Gabriel Goh et al.

title: A (Long) Peek into Reinforcement Learning
excerpt: Lilian Weng walks through RL fundamentals from bandits and MDPs through policy gradients, actor-critic methods, and deep RL algorithms with clear diagrams and citations. It is a survey rather than a reproduction study and predates LLM RLHF-specific practice.
author: Lilian Weng
coverAlt: Lilian Weng reinforcement learning overview cover

title: Leaderboards Are Harder Than They Look
excerpt: Hugging Face maintainers explain why public leaderboards drift from real capability—contamination, metric gaming, hidden preprocessing, and evaluation harness differences—and argue for task-specific, versioned benchmarks. The critique is ecosystem-wide rather than a single reproducible fix.
author: Hugging Face
